title: Theres must be a way to make actual decent VFX with AI.
author: zoaker
selftext:
i'm already tired of constantly getting very bad results, wasting a bunch of tokens to get low quality effects despite describing exactly and even making an tool for it for my game, but in the end it still looks hella bad

  
even forcing it to search for references, almost 10gb of screenshots of games's vfx effects, vids and others

  
and yet, still get bad results

  
is there an tool to actually make good vfx for magic, elements and such?

comments.author: MichaelEmouse
comments.body:
Use AI to build a VFX generator. You can play around with the parameters and toggles.

You can use interactive evolution to make the generator create N number of variations. Then you either keep and export it or you use that or those selected variants as the parents of the next generation.

  
Your first AI-built tool is going to be a learning opportunity. And many of the subsequent ones too, probably.

comments.author: VictorBuildsApps
comments.body:
One thing that helped on my UE jam game was giving the agent a picture of the goal instead of only a description. It took a real frame from a fight and edited the hit into it with image gen: a white crescent with a bright leading edge, small hot sparks with a white core that turn orange, and a dust ring on the floor for the punch. Then it rebuilt the effects from a script, recorded the fight at 60 fps and compared the frames with that concept before keeping a version.

The frame check catches things a description misses. The first hotter sparks came out as a fan of grey-white sticks, because the streak shader paints a white centre into anything that thin. Drawing them as small glow dots that fall as they cool fixed that.

comments.author: WalkinWhiskey
comments.body: people constantly run into these problems, whether it’s animation, whether it’s building, or whether it’s effects or sound. The problem is when you want the AI to give you the finished product without you having to pitch in your own creativity and your own ideas and passion into it, the reality is if you make a tool or you tell the AI to build you a VFX toolmaker, you can go crazy. You can tell it make all kinds of effects, right- Tell it, tell it to give you (or make you) 20 different effects to start off (however they look), tell it to to give you sliders for size, for speed, for swirl, for movement, for particles, for light, for everything, your sliders, your tools. If you want it, you can tell it, oh, allow me to overlay four of the same effects, allow me to turn on blend so those four effects can blend, and then u put particles, and then u put swirl, and then u put speed, and then I overlay three more effects, and then you’ll start getting some results you want, and that’s actually the best way that I found to build things that I want. make thing makers essentially. it’s even better when you look at an effect you have, and let’s say you send a picture to ChatGPT so that it makes you the picture of exactly what you want (like a high quality vfx) tell it what are the changes that you are seeing that you need implemented. Dont jump to a result. You might have to train your eyes for this, I for one did art, so whenever I get a picture or have a reference, I know exactly what to tell it. What angles it should take, what corners, the colors, the dimension, everything. But if you have an effect that you already know its what you want, but the effect that you output doesn’t match what you can do is simply look at specific details and go changing them one by one. If the effect that you like has a white rim light around the outline of the effect, tell it to add that to yours.
